title: Limit Order Matching Engine

statement.md: At the heart of every exchange sits a matching engine. Resting limit orders wait in the book; incoming market orders sweep the best prices on the opposite side until filled or the book runs dry. Priority is *price-time*: better prices trade first, and among orders at the same price the ones that arrived earlier trade first (FIFO). You will build a small but faithful single-instrument matching engine.

rows: Add a new resting limit order: side B or S, price in integer cents, positive qty. It never executes on arrival, even if it crosses the book, it just joins its price level.
Market order for qty shares. A market BUY sweeps the ask side from the lowest ask upward; a market SELL sweeps the bid side from the highest bid downward.

items: Price priority: a sweeping market order always trades at the best available price of the opposite side first, then moves to the next price when the level is exhausted.

Time priority: within one price level, resting orders trade in the order they were added (FIFO). A partially filled resting order keeps its place at the front of its queue with its remaining quantity.
Each trade fills min(remaining market qty, resting order qty) shares at the resting order's price.
One trade line is printed per (market order, resting order) match. A resting order nibbled by several market orders therefore appears in several trade lines.
A market order larger than the available opposite-side volume simply fills what is there (partial fill). A market order against an empty opposite side trades nothing.

statement.md: Print each trade the moment it happens as T price qty (price in dollars with exactly 2 decimals converted from integer cents, qty = shares filled in that match). After all events have been processed, print the remaining book top: BID x.xx (best remaining bid) or BID - when no bid remains, then ASK x.xx (best remaining ask) or ASK - when no ask remains.

statement.title: Levels vanish when drained
statement.md: When the last order of a price level is fully consumed the level disappears and the sweep continues at the next price. Forgetting to remove drained levels (or to re-evaluate the best price after every fill) is the classic bug in this problem, the sweep loop must look at the book state after EVERY trade, not once at the start.

inputFormat: Line 1: the integer n (number of events). Each of the next n lines is an event: either L side price qty (limit add) or M side qty (market order), where side is B or S, 1 <= price <= 10^6 is integer cents, and 1 <= qty <= 10^6.
outputFormat: All trade lines in the order the trades occur, each formatted T x.xx qty; then a line BID x.xx or BID -; then a line ASK x.xx or ASK -. Prices are integer cents printed as dollars with exactly 2 decimals.
constraints: Limit orders always rest; only market orders generate trades. Trade price = resting order's price.
The number of trade lines is bounded by the number of events, so output size is modest.

examples.explanation: M B 150 sweeps asks: 80 at 10.10, then 70 of the 120 at 10.15. M S 60 fills 60 of the bid of 100 at 10.00 (40 remain). L S 1008 40 rests. M B 30 fills 30 of those 40 at 10.08 (10 remain there). M S 500 sweeps bids: the remaining 40 at 10.00, then all 50 at 9.95. No bids remain; the asks still hold 10 at 10.08 and 50 at 10.15 -> best ask 10.08.

Two resting asks at 10.00 (10 then 20, FIFO). M B 15 fills 10 against the first order and 5 against the second. L B 990 30 rests. M S 25 fills 25 of that bid. M B 5 fills 5 of the remaining 15 at the 10.00 level. Final: bid 9.90 (5 left), ask 10.00 (10 left).

hints: Represent each side as an ordered map from price to a FIFO queue of remaining order quantities. For asks the best price is the smallest key; for bids the largest (an ordered map with a greater-than comparator makes the best bid begin()).

A market order is a while loop: while qty remains and the opposite side is non-empty, trade against the front order of the best level, then update the book (pop the queue, erase drained levels) and re-read the best price.
Track remaining quantity of the front order: full consumption pops it; a partial fill just reduces the front element, keeping its queue position.

editorial.md: Per side, the book is an ordered map price -> FIFO deque of remaining quantities. Ordered maps keep prices sorted, so the best ask is begin() on the ask map and the best bid is begin() on a bid map ordered with a greater comparator (or rbegin() on an ascending map). The deque per level preserves arrival order; its front element is the order that time priority trades first.

editorial.title: Sweeping with a market order
items: Take the opposite side's map; let best = its best key while the map is non-empty.
front = quantity of the front order at best; fill = min(front, remaining market qty). Emit T best fill (formatted from cents).
If fill == front, pop the front order; if its level deque is now empty, erase the price level entirely. Otherwise reduce the front element to front, fill; it stays at the head of the queue.
Re-read best (the map may have changed) and repeat while market qty > 0 and the side is non-empty.

editorial.title: Example walk-through
items: M B 150 sweeps asks: fills 80 at 1010 (T 10.10 80), level drained; fills 70 of the 120 at 1015 (T 10.15 70); market done.
M S 60 sweeps bids: fills 60 of the 100 at 1000 (T 10.00 60); 40 remains at the front of that level.
M B 30: fills 30 of the 40 resting at 1008 (T 10.08 30); 10 remain at the front of that level, a partial fill keeps its queue position.
M S 500 sweeps bids: fills the remaining 40 at 1000 (T 10.00 40), then all 50 at 995 (T 9.95 50); bids empty.
Final book: no bids; best ask is the remaining 10 at 1008 -> BID - / ASK 10.08.

editorial.md: Complexity: each event does O(log L) map work plus the trades it produces; every trade line corresponds to fully consuming one resting order (there are at most #L of those) or the final partial fill of one market order (at most #M of those). Total work is $O((n + T) \log L)$ with L live price levels, comfortably fast for n = 2000. The point of the problem is not speed but book-state discipline: erased levels, re-read best prices, and FIFO partial fills must all be exactly right.

editorial.title: Time priority survives partial fills
editorial.md: If a market order takes 6 of a resting 10, the remaining 4 keep the head of the level queue, a later market order meets those 4 before any order that arrived later. Implementing levels as plain quantity totals (losing per-order identity) breaks exactly this and fails the nibble tests.

solutions.python:
import sys
from collections import deque


def money(cents):
    return f"{cents // 100}.{cents % 100:02d}"


def main():
    lines = sys.stdin.read().split('\n')
    n = int(lines[0])
    book = {'B': {}, 'S': {}}  # side -> price -> FIFO queue of resting quantities
    out = []
    for line in lines[1:1 + n]:
        p = line.split()
        if p[0] == 'L':
            book[p[1]].setdefault(int(p[2]), deque()).append(int(p[3]))
            continue
        opp = 'S' if p[1] == 'B' else 'B'
        remaining = int(p[2])
        levels = book[opp]
        while remaining > 0 and levels:
            price = min(levels) if opp == 'S' else max(levels)
            queue = levels[price]
            while remaining > 0 and queue:
                fill = min(remaining, queue[0])
                out.append(f"T {money(price)} {fill}")
                remaining -= fill
                queue[0] -= fill
                if queue[0] == 0:
                    queue.popleft()
            if not queue:
                del levels[price]
    bid = max(book['B']) if book['B'] else None
    ask = min(book['S']) if book['S'] else None
    out.append('BID ' + (money(bid) if bid is not None else '-'))
    out.append('ASK ' + (money(ask) if ask is not None else '-'))
    print('\n'.join(out))


main()
